verdict.rationale: Braintrust documents agent-facing programmatic surfaces: an official MCP server and `bt` CLI let coding agents run evals, and the REST API and SDKs can create datasets and experiments and run evals from code. Reading eval results back programmatically is only implied, by API 'manage' of experiments and experiments being a comparable record, not explicitly documented as an agent workflow. missing for 10: explicit documentation of an agent retrieving experiment scores/results via MCP, CLI or API, an end-to-end agent create-dataset→run-eval→read-results example, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent create a dataset, trigger an eval run programmatically, and read back the results

citations.quote: Query production logs, author prompts and scorers, configure monitoring, and run evals from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, and any other MCP-compatible client.
You can use it to: Create and manage projects, experiments, and datasets
Log traces, manage prompts, create datasets, and run evals or experiments right from your code.
It lets you authenticate, trace coding-agent sessions, run evals, browse and query logs, sync data, and manage functions without leaving your terminal.
Experiments are the immutable, comparable record of your eval runs. Run them from code or in the UI
